metadata.title: THE LAST FLOOR — Episode 01: The Elevator That Shouldn’t Stop
metadata.description: Complete psychological-horror motion manga. 22 minutes, 4K UHD, 24 fps. English dialogue and panel lettering. Selective yellow supernatural accents.
metadata.keywords: manga motion-comic horror liminal elevator psychological-mystery

meta.name: source
meta.value: Texto colado(4).txt — screenplay supplied by user; original dialogue retained verbatim.

meta.name: delivery.status
meta.value: XML production instance only. Image, font, voice, ambience, music and effects paths must be populated before render. No asset hashes are fabricated.

meta.name: art.direction
meta.value: Original seinen horror manga; fine ink crosshatching, hard blacks, paper-white faces, coarse screentone shadows. Yellow #E3BC48 only on raincoat, floor 13 and supernatural seam. No imitation of a named artist. No embedded lettering in raster art.

meta.name: character.ren
meta.value: 16; slender, straight black fringe, watchful dark eyes; charcoal school jacket and pale shirt. Arrival uses light rain jacket. Keep each scene costume continuous.

meta.name: character.yuki
meta.value: Ren mother; adult with tied-back black hair, light blouse and charcoal cardigan; anxious expression. Eighteen-years-ago version visibly younger, same facial structure.

meta.name: character.aya
meta.value: 16; short angular black bob, sharp eyes, charcoal school uniform with pale collar; assured posture becoming visibly alarmed.

meta.name: character.nagai
meta.value: Elderly caretaker; stooped, deeply lined face, sparse white hair, worn dark work vest, small key ring.

meta.name: character.mari
meta.value: 27 in old photograph and apparition; long wet black hair, pale dress, bare feet. Human eyes in historical photograph; pure black eyes in bedroom elevator apparition.

meta.name: character.girl
meta.value: Child-sized supernatural figure in muted yellow raincoat; back turned. Head rotation is uncanny but no exposed injury or gore.

meta.name: asset.contract
meta.value: Every shot uses registered 4096x2304 background and transparent foreground plates, aligned pixel-for-pixel. Background contains environment and static figures; foreground contains only the named moving focal subject. Paint occluded areas fully. Leave 128px horizontal and 72px vertical overscan. Focal faces remain inside central 2800x1450; leave lower 400px for dialogue.

meta.name: motion.contract
meta.value: Each panel has a clipped art group; background and foreground receive different explicit transform curves for authored parallax. Panel borders and dialogue remain in screen space. Hard cuts are intentional; no procedural video generation during render.

meta.name: audio.contract
meta.value: 48 kHz, 24-bit WAV; mono voices and stereo sound/ambience/music. Each dialogue file is pre-edited to its declared duration including tail silence, starting at sample zero. No live TTS. Music and ambience stems are authored to their declared scene duration.

meta.name: voice.direction
meta.value: Ren quiet and observant; Yuki warm then terrified; Aya direct and hushed; Nagai low and deliberate; Mari affectionate with restrained menace; girl flat and distant. Original voices, no celebrity imitation.

meta.name: story.continuity
meta.value: The screenplay mixes ran away, disappeared and died before I was born. Preserve these as the inconsistent story Ren has been told, not an objective confirmed death. CCTV timestamp eighteen years ago is relative to narrative present, not a calendar date.

text.text: GIRL You got off too early.
EPISODE 01 The Elevator That Shouldn’t Stop
YUKI In Tokyo, cheap is a miracle.
NAGAI If the elevator ever stops somewhere you didn't choose...
YUKI He's trying to scare you.
AYA You're the transfer student from Kurosawa Apartments.
REN How do you know where I live?
REN That's a normal thing to say to someone you just met.
AYA Don't use the elevator after midnight.
REN The caretaker said something similar.
AYA Did he tell you about Floor Thirteen?
USER 114: Elevator stopped at 13. USER 77: There was a woman standing outside.
USER 201: My brother disappeared. USER 54: If you hear someone calling your name, don't answer.
AYA Six people disappeared from that building in twenty years.
REN My mother said she ran away.
AYA Your aunt lived in Kurosawa Apartments.
REN Why didn't you tell me?
YUKI Where did you get that?
YUKI We are not talking about this.
REN She disappeared from this building.
REN Why did we move here?
YUKI Never use the elevator after midnight.
REN What happened to Aunt Mari?
YUKI Three days after she disappeared.
YUKI She knocked on our mother's door at two in the morning.
YUKI (V.O.) And immediately knew it wasn't her.
YUKI It knew things Mari knew.
YUKI But it kept asking permission to come inside.
MARI (O.S.) You've gotten so big, Ren.
REN She died before I was born.
YUKI She shouldn't know your name.
MARI Ask her what happened on the thirteenth floor.
MARI (O.S.) She knows the way back.
DISPATCHER (V.O.) Emergency services. What's your location?

marker.label: COLD OPEN / The wrong floor
Black elevator interior. A fluorescent strip slowly reveals a tired office worker and his convenience-store bag.
Extreme close-up: finger pressing the worn seventh-floor button. Display begins at twelve.
Three narrow horizontal panels: eyes, descending counter, tightening fingers around a plastic bag.
The elevator stops. The worker looks up. A yellow number occupies an otherwise black panel.
Steel doors slide apart onto a corridor that extends far beyond the building. Central vanishing point.
A small girl in a yellow raincoat stands at the distant vanishing point, back turned. Empty corridor dominates.
Insert: the worker repeatedly presses CLOSE. The button sinks but the doors remain open.
Over the worker shoulder, the girl remains facing away. Her speech balloon is isolated above the corridor.
Close-up girl in yellow raincoat. Separate head cutout from neck pivot; her head tilts almost horizontal.
Blackness consumes the corridor. One final panel of the worker eye. Wet dragging and a scream; no gore.
TITLE / The Last Floor
Black paper. A narrow yellow elevator seam becomes the numeral thirteen.
A white manga title spreads across an ink-black page.
ACT ONE / Arrival
Wide low-angle view of rain-streaked concrete towers in a Tokyo-inspired city. Kurosawa tower has twenty stories.
Ren, sixteen, under a transparent umbrella; Yuki holds moving boxes beneath the entrance canopy.
Ren and Yuki pass through the glass entrance. Their reflections stretch over dark puddles.
High window detail: a pale human silhouette watches, then disappears behind a curtain.
ACT ONE / The caretaker
Lobby two-shot. Elderly Nagai hands Yuki a keycard. Ren notices the elevator panel.
Panel detail: one through twelve, then fourteen through twenty; conspicuous absent thirteen.
Ren presses the call button; it stays dark. Split panel: Nagai watches without blinking.
Nagai presses the same button. The lift arrives immediately. Thin diagonal panel across his hand.
Extreme close-up Nagai. Deep crosshatching under his eyes. The doors open behind Ren.
Nagai stares at Ren through the narrowing doorway. Steel leaves divide his face.
ACT ONE / A half-second mistake
Yuki laughs in the ascending elevator. Ren is reflected twice in brushed metal.
Insert of the floor display climbing. Ren watches the numbers.
The display briefly becomes thirteen; Ren catches the yellow reflection in his own eye.
Seven replaces thirteen. Ren turns to Yuki, whose gaze is elsewhere.
The elevator opens at eight. Normal light, uncomfortable silence.
ACT ONE / The scratches
Apartment 804 in daylight. Boxes on the floor; Yuki draws curtains onto an enormous gray city.
Ren enters his bedroom. A narrow closet and an empty wall feel disproportionately large.
Macro detail of dozens of pencil-thin tally scratches. Ren fingers trace the grooves.
Pencil writing emerges beneath the scratches. Keep the wall clean for a native XML text insert.
Ren turns toward the doorway at his mother call. Hold his worried profile.
Return to exactly the previous wall composition. The writing is gone; scratches remain.
ACT TWO / Aya
Busy classroom under gray daylight. Ren sits at a window, separated from classmates by empty desk space.
Aya, sixteen, sharp eyes and short black hair, drops into the adjacent desk.
Shot/reverse-shot in two asymmetric manga panels. Aya speaks without smiling.
Ren raises an eyebrow; Aya ignores the sarcasm.
Aya leans toward Ren. Insert on his fingers at the word eight.
Close-up Aya: confident expression collapses into urgent concern.
Aya whispers about floor thirteen. The classroom background loses detail to stark black.
Teacher silhouette enters. Aya sits back. The two teenagers face forward, conversation interrupted.
ACT TWO / The missing woman
School stairwell at lunch. Ren and Aya sit on concrete steps with convenience-store food.
Aya holds a phone displaying an old forum. Large blank screen area for typeset posts.
Second phone insert: old posts years apart, cropped profile icons and empty screen reserved for text.
Ren scrolls, unconvinced. Aya puts a finger against the screen to stop him.
Phone photograph: elevator steel door reflects a faceless dark figure. Progressive push into the reflection.
Aya explains the disappearances; Ren looks from the reflection to her face.
Missing-person poster on phone: portrait of Mari at twenty-seven, blank type area.
Ren face drains of color. Aya waits; a large empty panel separates them.
Ren stares at the photograph. Aya slowly locks her phone.
Hold a quiet stairwell wide shot. The two small figures sit surrounded by cold concrete.
ACT THREE / What came back
Evening kitchen. Yuki prepares dinner. Ren puts Mari missing-person photograph on the table.
Close-up Yuki hand, kitchen knife trembling above a cutting board.
Ren confronts Yuki across the table. She turns toward the counter.
Yuki grips the counter. Ren realizes she already knew.
Yuki turns, visibly terrified; space between mother and son opens into black gutters.
Ren anger gives way to concern. The kitchen is quiet around them.
Yuki speaks with tears in her eyes. Slow inward movement against a still background.
Flashback: grandmother apartment doorway at two in the morning. Wet, barefoot Mari stands outside smiling.
Flashback detail: Mari smile subtly widens beyond comfort. Keep eyes human here.
Back in the kitchen. Ren cannot understand; Yuki watches the apartment entrance.
Alternating slivers of Yuki eyes and the entrance lock.
The elevator chimes outside. Clock insert reveals an impossible jump from dinner to 1:13 A.M.
Kitchen fluorescent light dims once. Yuki is suddenly pale.
Apartment entrance from inside. Three slow knocks. Door grain forms vertical prison-like lines.
Yuki recognizes the voice beyond the locked door. Knife falls out of frame.
ACT FOUR / Permission
Ren and Yuki frozen in the dark apartment. Another knock; Yuki covers her mouth.
Ren approaches the door. Yuki grips his arm hard.
Round peephole view: empty corridor. Concentric black frame; no human visible.
A single enormous eye suddenly fills the peephole. Hard cut, no rapid flashing.
Ren jerks back. Offscreen Mari laughs almost affectionately.
Ren and Yuki face each other, shaken by what the voice knows.
Macro of locked doorknob slowly turning, stopping, then turning again. It never opens.
Ren phone vibrates. Unknown sender, blank screen reserved for native text.
Phone photograph of Ren and Yuki from behind, taken inside this apartment. They are wearing exactly the present outfits.
Ren turns into empty space behind him. Full-width silent panel.
A second message arrives. Yuki backs away from Ren.
Lights die. Yellow line under Ren bedroom door. An elevator chime comes from inside the apartment.
Bedroom doorway slides open to reveal an elevator. Mari stands inside, black eyes and the unchanged face from the old photo.
Yuki screams. Mari smiles without moving her body.
Invisible force grabs Yuki ankle. She falls; Ren seizes her arms.
Ren and Yuki struggle toward the elevator threshold. Her nails scrape the wood. Separate pair cutout for the dragging move.
Mari watches without moving. A narrow eye panel cuts across the struggle.
Ren looks down at Yuki. Her face shows guilt beneath terror. Doors slam; cut to absolute black.
DAWN / Eighteen years ago
Morning light. Ren and Yuki lie alive on the undamaged apartment floor. His bedroom is normal.
Ren sits up and opens one unread video message on his phone.
Security recording drawn as manga: young Yuki beside Mari in the same elevator. No speech, no recording audio.
CCTV floor counter changes to thirteen. Doors open and Mari steps outside.
Mari turns and silently speaks. Young Yuki reaches toward CLOSE.
Young Yuki presses CLOSE. Doors shut on Mari outside. Mari pounds at the narrowing opening.
Young Yuki covers her ears inside the elevator. Silent CCTV ends.
Ren looks at his sleeping mother. In the apartment window, an impossible elevator panel is reflected.
Close-up Ren listening. An unseen whisper behind him. Hard cut to black.
END CREDITS / Thousands of doors
Credits on black. A telephone begins ringing.
A barely visible endless corridor fills a narrow strip under the credits.
Thousands of closed doors recede into blackness; no caller shown.
The corridor narrows to a yellow seam. A final elevator chime, then silence.
